title: Simple Smurf shell: black theme, system font, left rail with Workflows / Runs / Settings
brief:
Desktop app (React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + lucide-react, folder desktop/). We are replacing the big Clutch UI (desktop/src/App.tsx, leave it and every old component untouched) with a new, very simple shell in a new folder desktop/src/smurf/. Look: black, quiet, like n8n's dark mode. One font: the system UI font.
1. Create desktop/src/smurf/theme.css with exactly these CSS variables on :root and base rules: --bg:#0a0a0b; --panel:#111113; --raised:#18181b; --line:#27272a; --text:#ededef; --muted:#8a8a93; --run:#60a5fa; --wait:#fbbf24; --ok:#34d399; --bad:#f87171; --g-senior:#a78bfa; --g-agent:#60a5fa; --g-human:#fbbf24; --g-verify:#34d399; --g-flow:#94a3b8; --g-workspace:#94a3b8; --g-output:#f472b6. html,body,#root {height:100%; margin:0; background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); font-family:"Segoe UI Variable Text","Segoe UI",system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif; font-size:13px; -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased}. .mono {font-family:"Cascadia Mono",Consolas,monospace}. Simple classes used by every view: .sm-btn (height 28px, padding 0 12px, radius 6px, border 1px solid var(--line), background var(--raised), color var(--text), hover background #222226, disabled opacity .4), .sm-btn-primary (background var(--text), color var(--bg), border-color var(--text)), .sm-input (height 28px, padding 0 8px, radius 6px, border 1px solid var(--line), background var(--bg), color var(--text); focus border-color var(--muted), outline none; also used on <select> and <textarea> where height:auto), .sm-label (font-size 11px, color var(--muted)), .sm-panel (background var(--panel), border 1px solid var(--line), radius 8px). :focus-visible {outline:2px solid var(--run); outline-offset:1px}. Also add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *{animation:none!important; transition:none!important} }`.
2. Create desktop/src/smurf/SmurfApp.tsx: full-window flex layout. Left rail 52px wide (background var(--panel), right border var(--line)) with the text 'S' as a small logo at top, then three icon buttons (lucide-react Workflow, Play, Settings; each with title + aria-label 'Workflows', 'Runs', 'Settings'); the active one has background var(--raised) and color var(--text), others var(--muted). At the bottom of the rail a 8px dot showing server health: poll `fetchServerHealth()` from '../services/serverUrl' every 10s; green (var(--ok)) when status ok and runner.connected, amber (var(--wait)) when ok but runner not connected, red (var(--bad)) on error; title text says which ('Server and runner connected', 'Runner not connected: run ./smurf.sh runner', 'Server not reachable'). Main area renders <WorkflowsView/>, <RunsView/> or <SettingsView/> (default Workflows), filling the remaining space (min-w-0, h-full, overflow hidden). Remember the active view in localStorage key 'smurf.view'.
3. Create placeholder views desktop/src/smurf/WorkflowsView.tsx, RunsView.tsx, SettingsView.tsx, each a named export (WorkflowsView, RunsView, SettingsView) rendering a centered muted line like 'Workflows' (later tasks fill them in).
4. desktop/src/main.tsx: import './smurf/theme.css' after './index.css' and render <SmurfApp/> instead of <App/> inside the existing <ServerGate> (keep StrictMode and ServerGate). Do not delete App.tsx.
Do not touch any other file.

title: Workflows: fast n8n-style canvas editor working directly on Smurf graphs
brief:
Desktop app (React 19 + TS + Tailwind v4 + @xyflow/react 12 + lucide-react, folder desktop/). A new simple shell lives in desktop/src/smurf/ (read SmurfApp.tsx and theme.css first; use its CSS variables and the .sm-btn / .sm-btn-primary / .sm-input / .sm-label / .sm-panel classes; black theme; no light colors). Build the Workflows screen as an n8n-like editor working DIRECTLY on the server's graph format, no Clutch canvas/compiler formats (do not import workflowFormat.ts or WorkflowOrchestration.tsx).
Server API (use `serverJson` and `serverFetch` from '../../services/serverUrl', paths are relative like '/api/nodes'; serverFetch needs the full URL `${getServerUrl()}/api/...`): GET /api/workflows/user -> { workflows: (Graph & { id: string })[] }; GET /api/workflows/user/:id -> { graph: Graph }; PUT /api/workflows/user/:id body { graph } -> { status: 'saved'|'invalid', problems: string[] }; GET /api/nodes -> NodeSpec[] = { type, label, group, description, ports: string[], params: { name, type: 'string'|'number'|'boolean'|'select', default?, options?, description }[] }[]. Graph = { name: string; description?: string; start: string; nodes: { id: string; type: string; name?: string; params?: Record<string, unknown>; position?: [number, number] }[]; edges: { from: string; port?: string; to: string }[] } (omitted port means 'out'). Groups: senior, flow, human, output, agent, workspace, verify.
1. desktop/src/smurf/canvas/graph.ts (pure, no React): types Graph, GraphNode, GraphEdge, NodeSpec; `toFlow(g, specs)` -> { nodes, edges } for @xyflow/react: node type 'card', id = graph id, position from g position or an automatic left-to-right layout (breadth-first from g.start, 260px between levels, 110px between rows), data = { graphNode, spec, isStart }; edge id `${from}:${port}->${to}`, sourceHandle = port, label = port unless 'out', type 'smoothstep'. `fromFlow(nodes, edges, base: Graph)` -> Graph (positions rounded to integers, keeps name/description/start, edges from sourceHandle). `addNode(g, spec, position)` -> new Graph with a new unique id (spec.type's last segment + number, e.g. 'plan2'), params defaulted from spec param defaults (skip undefined). `removeNode(g, id)` removes the node and its edges (if it was start, start becomes the first remaining node or ''). `connect(g, from, port, to)` adds an edge, replacing any existing edge from the same node+port. `validateLocal(g, specs)` -> string[] (missing start, unknown type, edge to missing node, port not in spec.ports) mirroring the server rules.
2. graph.test.ts (vitest): toFlow/fromFlow round trip keeps nodes, params, edges and ports; addNode unique ids and defaults; removeNode cleans edges and start; connect replaces same-port edge; validateLocal catches each problem.
3. NodeCard.tsx: memo'ed custom node, 200x56, radius 10px, background var(--raised), 1px border var(--line) (selected: var(--text)). Left: 36x36 rounded square tinted with the group color (`var(--g-${group})` at ~18% via color-mix, icon in full group color; lucide icons by group: senior Brain, agent Bot, human UserCheck, verify ShieldCheck, flow GitBranch, workspace FolderGit2, output FileText). Right: name (node.name or spec.label) 13px, below it the type in 11px var(--muted) .mono. Start node shows a small 'start' tag. One target Handle on the left; one source Handle per spec port on the right, spaced vertically, each with a tiny 10px port label when there is more than one port. Optional data.status ('running'|'waiting'|'completed'|'pending') draws a 2px ring in var(--run)/var(--wait)/var(--ok) (pending: none); running ring pulses with a simple CSS animation.
4. FlowCanvas.tsx: props { graph, specs, readOnly?, status?: Record<string, string>, selectedId?, onSelect?(id|null), onChange?(g) }. PERFORMANCE IS THE MAIN POINT: define `const nodeTypes = { card: NodeCard }` at module level; keep nodes/edges in useNodesState/useEdgesState and apply ALL changes with the provided handlers (never drop dimension/selection changes); only call onChange(fromFlow(...)) when a drag ends (change.dragging === false), on connect, and on delete, not on every mouse move; rebuild flow nodes from props only when the graph identity or specs change; status changes update only node data via setNodes(map). ReactFlow settings: colorMode 'dark', fitView once, minZoom .2, snapToGrid [20,20], deleteKeyCode ['Delete','Backspace'] (not when readOnly), onlyRenderVisibleElements, proOptions { hideAttribution: true }, <Background variant dots gap 20 size 1 color '#26262a'/>, <Controls showInteractive={false}/>, style background var(--bg). Override xyflow's controls and edges to dark: edge stroke '#52525b' 1.5px, selected edge var(--text). readOnly: no drag, no connect, no delete, still selectable via onSelect.
5. NodePanel.tsx: right panel 300px (.sm-panel style but full height, left border only) for the selected node: type + description from the spec, Name input, one control per spec param (text / number / checkbox / select, help text in .sm-label, default as placeholder; empty input removes the param), 'Set as start' button, 'Delete node' button. Calls onChange(updatedGraph).
6. WorkflowsView.tsx (replace the placeholder, keep the named export): three columns. Left 220px list of workflows (name, muted node count), a 'New' button that copies the 'default' graph under a name the user types (inline input, id = slug of the name) and PUTs it; selected row background var(--raised). Center: top bar with the workflow name, an 'Add node' button that opens a small searchable popover listing node specs grouped by group (click adds the node at the canvas center-ish and selects it), problems count from validateLocal (click shows the list), 'Discard' and 'Save' (.sm-btn-primary, disabled when unchanged). Save PUTs the graph; on 'invalid' show the server problems under the top bar in var(--bad); on success show 'Saved' for 2s. Canvas fills the rest. Right: NodePanel when a node is selected. Empty states say what to do ('Pick a workflow on the left', 'No workflows yet. Start the runner: ./smurf.sh runner'). Keep it simple; no other features.

title: Runs: start a run and watch it on the canvas
brief:
Desktop app (folder desktop/). New simple shell in desktop/src/smurf/ (read SmurfApp.tsx, theme.css, canvas/FlowCanvas.tsx and canvas/graph.ts first; black theme, use the .sm-* classes and CSS variables; reuse FlowCanvas in readOnly mode with its `status` prop). Do not import the old Clutch components or services/clutchState.ts.
Server API (serverJson/serverFetch/getServerUrl/serverWebSocketUrl from '../../services/serverUrl'): GET /api/workspaces -> { workspaces: { id, workspace_path, name }[], active_id }; GET /api/runs/history?workspace_id=ID -> { sessions: { run_id, title, status, workspace_id, created_at, updated_at }[] }; POST /api/sessions body { workspace_id, title } -> { run_id }; GET /api/seniors -> { default: string[], options: { key, tier, billing, cooling }[] }; PUT /api/sessions/:id/senior body { senior: key } (before the first message); GET /api/runs/:id/state -> state (the server's real shape is UiState in orchestrator/src/server/projection.ts; read it, define your own narrow type, use only these fields): { status: 'idle'|'running'|'awaiting_human'|'passed'|'failed', workflow_id, active_node_id, visited_nodes?: string[], messages: { id, agent: string, time: string, text: string }[], terminal_logs: string[], pending_subtasks: { id, title, status, summary? }[], waiting?: { kind, question, options: string[] } | null, session_cost_usd, error? }; GET /api/workflows/user/:id -> { graph }; GET /api/workflows/user -> { workflows }; GET /api/nodes -> specs. WebSocket `await serverWebSocketUrl('/ws/runs/' + runId)` accepts JSON messages: first message { text, senior?, workflow_id? } starts the run; { action: 'human_decision', decision } answers a gate; { action: 'stop_run' } stops it.
1. runs/runApi.ts: small typed wrappers for the calls above, plus `sendToRun(runId, payload)` that opens the WebSocket, sends one JSON payload once open, and closes after 500ms (resolves when sent, rejects on error/timeout 5s); `nodeStatuses(state)` -> Record<nodeId, 'completed'|'running'|'waiting'|'pending'> using stepStatus from '../../services/stepStatus' for every visited node and the active node; `isLive(status)` true for running/awaiting_human.
2. runApi.test.ts: nodeStatuses and isLive.
3. RunsView.tsx (replace the placeholder, keep the named export RunsView): left 260px column: project <select> (workspaces, default active_id), 'New run' button, list of runs for that project (title, status dot colored run/wait/ok/bad, relative time), selected row var(--raised). 'New run' shows in the main area a simple form: workflow <select> (default 'default'), senior <select> (options, default the first of `default`), request <textarea> (6 rows), 'Start run' (.sm-btn-primary). Start = POST /api/sessions {workspace_id, title: first 60 chars of request} -> PUT senior -> sendToRun(run_id, { text, senior, workflow_id }) -> select the run. Selected run main area: header (title, status, cost, 'Stop' when live), then a split: top 55% read-only FlowCanvas of the run's workflow graph with status from nodeStatuses; bottom: when state.waiting is set, show waiting.question and a row of buttons for each waiting.options entry (sendToRun human_decision with that option); then two tabs 'Messages' (each message's text with its agent name and time as a small label, newest at bottom, auto-scroll; render text as preformatted wrapped text, no markdown library) and 'Log' (terminal_logs in .mono 11px). Poll GET state every 2s while live, stop polling when not live (one more fetch at the end). Keep everything plain and small.

title: Settings: server connection and models
brief:
Desktop app (folder desktop/). New simple shell in desktop/src/smurf/ (read SmurfApp.tsx and theme.css first; black theme; use the .sm-* classes and CSS variables only). Replace the placeholder desktop/src/smurf/SettingsView.tsx (keep the named export SettingsView) with one scrollable column (max-width 760px, padding 24px) of two sections, each with a 15px heading:
1. 'Connection': server URL and token inputs prefilled from getServerUrl()/getServerToken() ('../services/serverUrl'; token input type password with a Show toggle), 'Test' button using checkServerConnection(url, token) showing the result in one line (ok in var(--ok), error in var(--bad)), and 'Save' calling saveServerConfig({url, token}) then window.location.reload(). Below, one muted line with the runner status from fetchServerHealth() (connected host, or 'Runner not connected: run ./smurf.sh runner').
2. 'Models': fetchModels() from '../services/smurfApi' -> a plain table (columns: model key in .mono, adapter, tier, Free/Paid, status: 'cooling down' in var(--wait) when cooling, else 'ready' in var(--muted)), grouped by adapter with a small muted group row, a 'Refresh' button that calls GET /api/models?refresh=1 via serverJson and reloads the table (show 'Refreshing...' while busy). Table rows 30px, 1px var(--line) separators, no zebra colors.
Only change SettingsView.tsx.
